sources.citation: Lama, Ziwo Qiu-Fuyuan. 2012. Subgrouping of Nisoic (Yi) languages. PhD dissertation, University of Texas at Arlington.
Pelkey, Jamin R. 2011. A Phula Comparative Lexicon: Phola, Phuza, Muji, Phowa, Azha. SIL Language and Culture Documentation and Description 18. Dallas: SIL International. 144 pp.
sources.note: SILENT. Phuma-YZT is a datapoint (p.~3 key '屏边县白河乡岩子头'); sec. 4.6 pp. 15-16: 'Bokha [ybk] and Phuma [ypm] form their own micro-clade within Muji based on the aspiration of bilabial stops...'. Muji-clade sketch sec. 3.3 'Southern Muji phonology in brief' pp. 8-9 is of Muji-PJZ, not Phuma; 0 occurrences of stress/accent/prominence in the book.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority / Pelkey, Jamin R. 2007. Change Request 2007-104: create [ypm] Phuma (adopted 2008-01-14), with Request for New Language Code Element [ypm]. SIL International. 8 + 5 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on phonology: identity, location (east-central Pingbian County), 8,000 speakers, autonym Phuma/Phupa, alt. names Muji, Phula, Paotlo, Shaoji Phula, Hei Muji, Phuli; closest = Bokha (RTT 0.40); sources cited = PBMZ 1990, PBXZ 1999 gazetteers, Pelkey forthcoming 2008 PhD.

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2007. Muji's mirrored merger: correlative redistribution of checked tone classes in a newly defined Burmic cluster. Mon-Khmer Studies 37: 179-195.
sources.note: SILENT. Phuma-YZT is one of the Muji-cluster datapoints (Table 3 'bird'; datapoint list 'Phuma: Yanzitou village, Baihe district, Pingbian county'); the sec. 2 phonology sketch is of Muji-PJZ only; tone classes only, no stress/accent statement.

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2011. Dialectology as Dialectic: Interpreting Phula Variation. TiLSM 229. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton. Ch. 5 'Phula phonologies: Five representative sketches' (pp. 223-270) and ch. 6 sec. 6.3 Muji clade (pp. 271-351).
